# Subject reclassification

<!-- Generated by tools/coherent-model/subjects/report.mjs from classification.mjs. Edit the classification, then regenerate. -->

The canonical model is reorganized by **subject**: an area of reusable business knowledge with one coherent responsibility (the *subject data areas* of the Data Model Resource Book). **Industries** (health care, crane rental, travel, …) are industry patterns: they select and explain subjects, and name what an application typically adds. The model carries **common models only**; an application adds its own concepts in its own Specs.

Every current concept is classified:

| Fate | Meaning | Concepts |
|---|---|---|
| **Common** | kept as it is, in its subject | 114 |
| **Merged** | the same concept under another name in another industry: merged into one common concept; its name becomes an alias | 196 |
| **Specialization** | a variation many applications of an industry need, adding reusable knowledge: kept, specializing a common concept | 48 |
| **Industry subject** | kept in a subject one industry owns (health care, insurance, financial accounts, networks, production, travel) | 94 |
| **Application detail** | needed by one kind of business only, or adding nothing an application could not define: leaves the model, named in one line in its industry pattern | 68 |
| **Modeling pattern** | a data-migration concern, not business knowledge: moves to modeling-patterns/ | 33 |
| **New** | a common concept Administration only named as a candidate: defined now | 13 |

From 553 concepts in 23 domains, plus 13 new, to **307 concepts in 24 subjects**.

## Subjects

| Subject | Responsibility | Concepts |
|---|---|---|
| **Parties and Roles** (`party`) | Who takes part: persons, organizations and their units, the roles they play in a context, their relationships (reporting among them), contacts, and customer and supplier accounts. | 13 |
| **Locations and Sites** (`location`) | Where things happen: geographic locations, facilities with their buildings and spaces, the sites where work or service is delivered, and their assessment. | 6 |
| **Classification** (`classification`) | Governed vocabularies and categories, and their assignment to anything. | 3 |
| **Products, Offerings, and Prices** (`product`) | What is provided and on what terms: products, versions and components, services, offerings, channels, catalogs, promotions, prices and price rules. | 16 |
| **Agreements and Entitlements** (`agreement`) | Rights and obligations: agreements of every kind, their parties and terms, commitments, entitlements, subscriptions, allowances, warranties, service levels. | 12 |
| **Requests, Quotes, and Orders** (`request`) | What is asked for and accepted: requests and applications, quotes, orders and order lines, changes and cancellations. | 13 |
| **Fulfillment and Logistics** (`fulfillment`) | How what was ordered reaches its recipient: fulfillment, fulfillment orders, shipments, packages, routes, delivery, and returns. | 11 |
| **Work and Projects** (`work`) | Work done: work efforts and orders, projects and tasks, assignments, service events, deliverables, outcomes, and status. | 12 |
| **Cases and Decisions** (`case`) | Managed matters and their resolution: cases, disputes, incidents, exceptions, approvals, authorizations, and decisions. | 7 |
| **Documents and Evidence** (`document`) | Recorded information: documents, notes, evidence, and communications. | 3 |
| **Scheduling and Reservations** (`scheduling`) | Time and capacity commitments: demand, requirements and constraints, schedules, appointments, reservations, attendance. | 8 |
| **Workforce** (`workforce`) | The people who do the work: workers and their employment, jobs and positions, skills and qualifications, and the time they record. | 9 |
| **Resources and Assets** (`resource`) | What capacity is drawn from: resources and their capabilities and availability, equipment and its models, components, configurations, maintenance, inventory. | 12 |
| **Quality and Inspection** (`quality`) | Whether something meets its requirements: quality plans, inspections and their results, nonconformances, corrective actions. | 5 |
| **Billing and Payments** (`finance`) | Money owed and settled: charges, invoices, billing accounts, payments and their methods and authorizations, refunds, adjustments, commissions, settlements, reconciliations, expenses. | 14 |
| **Accounting** (`accounting`) | Recording business transactions: the chart of accounts, accounting periods, ledger accounts, journal entries and their posting, receivables and payables. | 7 |
| **Measurement and Usage** (`measurement`) | What is measured and consumed: measures, measurements, usage records, analytic facts. | 4 |
| **Information Governance** (`information`) | How information is identified, owned, protected, and kept: external identifiers, matching and golden records, systems of record, data quality, consent, access, provenance, audit, retention. | 16 |
| **Health Care** (`care`) | Care of a patient: patients and providers, encounters and episodes, conditions, observations, diagnoses, procedures, care plans and goals, orders, care teams. One industry owns it. | 20 |
| **Insurance Coverage and Claims** (`coverage`) | Protection against loss and its claims: insurance products and policies, coverage and its terms, underwriting, premium, loss events, claims and their assessment, reserves, recoveries, reinsurance. Shared by insurance and health care. | 31 |
| **Financial Accounts** (`accounts`) | Financial positions and their movements, as a financial institution keeps them: accounts and balances, holds and limits, instructions and transactions, payment orders and clearing, credit and loans, instruments and trades. One industry owns it. | 26 |
| **Service Provisioning and Networks** (`network`) | Delivering a technical service: service and resource specifications, service instances, network resources and endpoints, provisioning and activation, alarms and outages. | 26 |
| **Production** (`production`) | Making products: routings and operations, work centers, bills of material, production orders and runs, output, scrap and rework, genealogy. | 17 |
| **Travel** (`travel`) | Travel itineraries and bookings: itineraries, segments, bookings and tickets, traveler documents, disruptions and reaccommodation. One industry owns it. | 16 |

- **Equipment Service** ([pattern](../industry-patterns/equipment-service.md)): Equipment Category.

## To modeling patterns

Legacy conversion is a modeling concern (source structures, mappings, migration runs, cutover), not a subject. Its 33 migration concepts move to a *Data Migration* modeling pattern; its identity, ownership, and data-quality concepts join Information Governance.

Source Dataset, Source Entity, Source Field, Source Record, Canonical Concept, Canonical Attribute, Target Store, Target Record, Mapping Specification, Field Mapping, Value Mapping, Transformation Rule, Default Rule, Data Profile, Semantic Issue, Migration Plan, Migration Wave, Migration Batch, Migration Item, Validation Result, Conversion Error, Exception, Resolution, Lineage Record, Reconciliation, Control Evidence, Synchronization Contract, Change Capture, Conflict, Cutover Event, Rollback Point, Archive Package, Decommission Plan.

## Administration

`model/domains/administration/` held only candidate lists for Organization, Human Resources, Facilities, and Accounting: named, never defined, and not in the model. They are common to every business, so they join the subjects: organization structure in Parties and Roles, the workforce and the ledger as subjects of their own (Workforce, Accounting), facilities in Locations and Sites. Concepts the model already had take their place (Worker from Technician and Professional, Qualification, Skill, Time Entry; Ledger Account, Journal Entry, Posting Batch from Financial Services; Facility; Invoice, Payment, Expense, Customer Account). The rest are defined now:

| Concept | Subject | From | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| Organization Unit | Parties and Roles | Organization | A part of an Organization with its own responsibility: a department, business unit, team, or branch. |
| Reporting Relationship | Parties and Roles | Organization | A Party Relationship stating who reports to whom, between Positions or Organization Units. |
| Supplier Account | Parties and Roles | Accounting | The governed commercial relationship with a Party that supplies Products or Services; the counterpart of Customer Account. |
| Employment | Workforce | Human Resources | The time-bounded relationship under which a Worker works for an Organization: employee, contractor, or volunteer. |
| Job | Workforce | Human Resources | A defined kind of work an Organization recognizes, with its duties and requirements. |
| Position | Workforce | Human Resources | A place in an Organization Unit for one Worker, of a Job, which may be vacant. |
| Position Requirement | Workforce | Human Resources | A Skill, Qualification, or condition a Position requires. |
| Building | Locations and Sites | Facilities | A structure at a Facility or Site. |
| Space | Locations and Sites | Facilities | An identifiable area within a Building or Facility: a floor, room, bay, bed, or desk. |
| Chart of Accounts | Accounting | Accounting | The governed set of Ledger Accounts an Organization records its transactions in. |
| Accounting Period | Accounting | Accounting | A bounded period for which transactions are recorded, closed, and reported. |
| Receivable | Accounting | Accounting | An amount owed to the Organization, recorded from an Invoice or other claim until settled. |
| Payable | Accounting | Accounting | An amount the Organization owes, recorded from a supplier invoice or other obligation until paid. |

The candidates not taken: Department and Business Unit (kinds of Organization Unit), Employee (a kind of Employment), Job Classification (a Classification), Competency (a Skill), Workplace and Facility Assignment (a Site; an Assignment), Organizational Location (a Facility), Account (a Ledger Account), Ledger (the Chart of Accounts), Journal (Journal Entries in a Posting Batch). The folder is removed.

## Open questions

1. **Merge names.** Where a merge creates a new common name (*Customer*, *Worker*, *Work Order*, *Price List*, *Usage Record*, *Site*, *Application*), is the name right?
2. **Industry subjects.** Health Care, Insurance Coverage and Claims, Financial Accounts, Service Provisioning, Production, and Travel are owned by one industry each (Coverage is shared with health care). Keep them as subjects, or move what is not common into the patterns as application detail too?
3. **New concepts.** The 13 concepts defined from Administration's candidates are written short; do they say what you mean (above)?

Decided: the merge names, the industry subjects, and the renames stand as proposed; physical therapy leaves the model (what it shared with other domains stays, as aliases of the common concepts), and its pattern names its concepts.
